plotting_plan.title: The anklet case: one ledger, three worlds
plotting_plan.objective: Teaser diagram. Left: SIL-16 records along story time (show to goldsmith, goldsmith takes queen's anklet, accusation 'Kovalan stole it' [claimed], king accepts, conditional order, killing, king rejects at SIL-20). Right: three folds at t=16.5 — the text's world (holder = goldsmith), the king's view (holder = Kovalan), and a naive triple graph that promotes the claim. Shows that an n-ary event node for the lie is indistinguishable from a true one, while the mood gate keeps it out of state.

plotting_plan.title: Accuracy, claim leakage and encoding size across representations
plotting_plan.objective: Scatter plot: x = statements (held-out encoding size, log scale), y = held-out accuracy; marker colour/shape encodes leak rate (0 vs >0). Seven methods. Shows event nodes leak as much as flat triples, standards and ledger tie at 1.0 but ledger uses 45% of the statements.

plotting_plan.title: What carries the load: feature ablation and cross-epic composition
plotting_plan.objective: Two-panel horizontal bar chart. Left: questions right (of 121) and false facts when each feature is removed (mood is the only one that creates false facts; birth label changes nothing). Right: cross-epic transfer, per-verb templates vs composer: right and false facts for SIL->MAN and MAN->SIL.

plotting_plan.title: Does the LLM read the verse or recall the story?
plotting_plan.objective: Grouped bar chart. Pilot (famous cantos, same-line match): few, zero, notext, masked recall with chance bands. Stage test (lesser-known cantos): few .804 vs notext .429 vs chance mean .452 (97.5th pct .554). Shows that on lesser-known cantos without verse recall falls to chance.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Knowledge graphs and graph-based retrieval are increasingly built from narrative and literary text by LLMs, and narrative is dominated by statements that are not facts (claims, lies, orders, beliefs, dreams).
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Standard KG representations, including n-ary event reification, have no notion of who says something and in what mood, so character claims are promoted to facts (epistemic leakage); this is measured here on two classical Tamil epics, a low-resource classical language with no prior structured resource.
search_directions: Knowledge graph construction from narrative or literary text, and LLM-based knowledge graph construction
Event factuality and source-relative factuality annotation (FactBank) and belief/attribution in NLP
Computational literary studies / narrative understanding surveys

NLP for Tamil and low-resource classical languages

related_work_strategy.overview: Three clusters: (1) representing statements beyond triples, (2) narrative and literary knowledge graphs, (3) extraction and question answering with LLMs over graphs. Plus text reuse.

section_plan.plan: Hook (said is not done) → epistemic leakage measured → ledger+fold+composer → key numbers: event nodes leak .75; ledger ties a full standards model at 45% statements; mood ablation 26 false facts; composer cross-epic 0 false facts vs 24; 57% of plain paths refused; held-out QA 19/20 vs 12; full-coverage resource 10,209 lines with LLM drafting gated by a pre-registered test (.804 vs .429 notext).

Open with the goldsmith's accusation SIL-16-0145 and his secret SIL-16-0127. Define epistemic leakage. Show that n-ary reification makes a lie neater. Three questions: (Q1) which representations leak, (Q2) what minimal structure prevents it, (Q3) can it scale to a whole classical text with LLMs without leaking. Contributions list. Honest framing: expressivity isn't the claim.

section_plan.plan: Three lessons: (i) truth is a property of telling, not of structure; (ii) the bottleneck is mood detection, which surface cues cannot do and LLMs can partly do; (iii) for famous texts, controls for recall are necessary.
Single annotator, self-written questions, small held-out sets, same-family judge, scholar review pending, echo finder unproven, no dense retrieval, Wikidata errors.
